newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX soars above 8,000pts on earnings hopes.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX soars above 8,000pts on earnings hopes.

text.p: Hungarian shares roared ahead on Tuesday, surging above the 8,000 points for the the first time as investors anticipated more good earnings reports to come as the August 15 deadline nears.
The BUX index finished at 8,168.13 points, up 187.01 points or 2.34 percent. During the session it set a trading high of 8,280.89 points.
But analysts think a downward correction must come at one stage.

"The short-term is looking good, a possibility of a minor correction in the next couple of weeks, but moving into a neutral stance by the year-end," said Stephen O'Sullivan, head of eastern European research at MC-BBL Securities in London.
First half earnings reports, which have to come through the market by August 15, might give reason for some profit-taking, he added.
But for the time being earnings expectations are driving the market into the positive direction, traders said earlier.
On Tuesday, oil and gas company MOL was one of the market's strong gainers.
"When foreigners buy MOL, their purpose differs from that of domestic clients," Gabor Sitanyi, analyst at ING Barings in London told Reuters earlier.
"Domestic clients buy it for its second quarter, while foreigners buy MOL for its last quarter," he added.
Traditionally, the first and the fourth quarters are the strongest for MOL.
MOL finished at a new closing high of 5,105 forints, up 115, coming down from a peak of 5,390 set on Tuesday.
On the derivatives market BUX index futures reflected changes on the spot market, prompting immediate clearings due to rises above the 200 point limit, a futures trader said.
"As the share market fell so did the futures market," said Gabor Legindi of Eastbrokers.
The most actively traded December maturity finished at 8,760 points, up 164.5 points from Monday's settlement of 8,595.5 points.

On the spot market the few losers included hotel firm Danubius after it boosted its stake in Helia Hotel to 99.94 percent, exercising its option rights set in a deal last year. Danubius finished at 6,450 forints, down 50.
